title: Dark Rye Bread
description: Full credit to bakers who perfected this rich, flavourful loaf — dense, dark, and deeply satisfying.

method.instruction: In a large mixing bowl, combine warm water, vegetable oil, and molasses. Stir until well mixed.
Add instant yeast to the liquid and let sit for 5 minutes until slightly foamy.
In a separate bowl, whisk together Baker's flour, rye flour, vital wheat gluten, cocoa powder, salt, and bread improver.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet mixture, stirring until a sticky, dark dough forms.

Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface (or in a stand mixer with a dough hook) for 10-12 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough will be dense but should not stick excessively to your hands.
Place dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a damp tea towel, and let rise in a warm place for 1.5-2 hours or until doubled in size.
Punch down the dough and shape into a tight oval or round loaf. Place in a greased loaf tin or on a lined baking tray.
Cover and let rise for another 45-60 minutes until puffy.
Brush the top of the loaf with water and make a few shallow slashes with a sharp knife.
Bake for 35-40 minutes until the crust is dark and firm, and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.
Remove from oven and cool on a wire rack for at least 30 minutes before slicing.

notes.title: Vital Wheat Gluten
notes.content: Rye flour is low in gluten, so vital wheat gluten helps give the loaf structure and prevents it from being too dense or crumbly.

notes.title: Darker Color
notes.content: For an even darker loaf, add an extra 10g of cocoa powder. The molasses and cocoa create the characteristic dark color and rich flavor.

notes.title: Best Served
notes.content: This bread is excellent toasted with butter, or served with smoked fish, pickles, and cream cheese for a traditional pairing.
